domain: International Law / Colonial History / Sovereignty Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494), examining papal authority as the legitimating basis for Iberian division of the New World. The treaty established a demarcation line ~370 leagues west of Cape Verde, with Spain claiming exclusive rights west and Portugal claiming rights east, both grounding territorial sovereignty in papal grant rather than indigenous sovereignty or prior occupation.

key_entities: Pope Alexander VI (Borgia pope; issued Inter caetera bulls 1493)
Spanish Crown (Castile and Aragon; beneficiary west of line)
Portuguese Crown (beneficiary east of line; prior Treaty of Alcáçovas 1479)
Indigenous populations (non-Christian peoples subject to conquest)
Rival European powers (France, England, Netherlands; excluded from papal grant)
Papal See (Rome; claimed universal temporal authority over non-Christian lands)
key_tensions: Papal authority vs secular sovereignty (Rome's claim to grant territorial rights vs emerging state sovereignty)
Prior discovery vs papal grant (Portuguese exploration-based claims vs papal bulls)
Christian vs non-Christian land rights (papal doctrine vs indigenous territorial sovereignty)

omegas.description: Does indigenous_sovereignty_erasure warrant independent constraint axis, or is it structurally derivative of the papal authority mountain? If indigenous peoples had legal standing, the entire kernel collapses—suggesting erasure is prerequisite, not consequence.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + deferred axis indigenous_sovereignty_erasure

omegas.description: Was Tordesillas ever binding on non-signatories (France, England, Netherlands)? If not, Portuguese reading's victim set (rival_european_powers) may be mislabeled—constraint operated only within Iberian dyad, not globally.
How enforceable was the demarcation line given 1494 cartographic precision? If practically unenforceable, both readings may be post-hoc legitimations of conquest rather than operational constraints.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + epsilon_bin classification uncertainty

omegas.description: Is papal_temporal_authority a true Mountain (theological necessity for Catholic powers) or a Piton (contingent on Catholic dominance)? Protestant Reformation and Westphalian sovereignty reclassify it as historically bounded Piton.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: papal_temporal_authority_mountain classified as mountain but may be historically bounded piton contingent on Catholic theological-political dominance. Protestant powers rejected this authority basis ab initio. Generated omega_papal_authority_persistence to bound this uncertainty.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The papal bull Inter caetera and Treaty of Tordesillas establish a fixed demarcation line as the shared commitment—a geographic partition grounding territorial legitimacy claims for Iberian powers
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Papal See claims universal temporal authority over non-Christian lands; interpretive legitimacy derives from theological doctrine of papal supremacy and Christian evangelization duty
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Founding Text (Type 1): fixed demarcation line functions as immutable founding text; revisions (e.g., line adjustments) required new treaties rather than interpretive flexibility

readings.commitment: Papal grant as license for territorial conquest and indigenous subjugation west of line
readings.authority_grounding: Pure papal grant; theological duty to evangelize; Requerimiento as legal ritual
readings.expected_structural_delta: High epsilon snare; victim set = indigenous populations west of line; beneficiary = Spanish colonial administration; extractiveness manifest in encomienda system and forced conversion

readings.commitment: Papal treaty as confirmation of prior exploration rights and exclusion of European rivals east of line
readings.authority_grounding: Prior discovery (Treaty of Alcáçovas 1479) ratified by papal authority; trade monopoly enforcement
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate epsilon tangled rope; victim set = rival European powers (not indigenous populations as primary target); beneficiary = Portuguese Estado da Índia; extractiveness in trade monopoly rather than land conquest

axiom_contradictions.basis: Spanish reading treats papal authority as sufficient ground for conquest regardless of prior occupation; Portuguese reading treats prior discovery as necessary precondition that papal authority merely ratifies. No coherent framework holds both 'papal grant creates territorial right ex nihilo' and 'papal grant only confirms pre-existing discovery-based right' simultaneously.
